candidate_overview.interview_focus_paradigm: High emphasis on Core Computer Science Fundamentals (DSA, OOP, System Internals), Low-Level Object-Oriented Design (OOD), and behavioral assessment using Amazon Leadership Principles.

identified_topics.name: Java
identified_topics.why_interview_relevant: Java is heavily utilized in Amazon backend services. As an SDE-1 candidate, a deep understanding of Java language internals, memory management, and collection frameworks is expected.

identified_topics.name: Spring Boot
identified_topics.why_interview_relevant: Spring Boot indicates experience in enterprise-level Java backend development. The candidate's understanding of dependency injection, application configuration, and REST API controllers will be assessed.

identified_topics.name: MySQL
identified_topics.why_interview_relevant: Relational databases are fundamental to enterprise transactional systems. An interviewer will explore schema design, normalization, ACID transactions, and index optimization.

identified_topics.name: AI Interview System
identified_topics.why_interview_relevant: This is the core project on the resume. An interviewer will use this to test the candidate's end-to-end ownership, engineering design decisions, and how they handled technical challenges and bottlenecks.

inferred_topics.name: Data Structures & Algorithms (DSA)
inferred_topics.why_interview_relevant: The primary filter in Amazon technical recruitment. SDE-1 candidates must demonstrate strong algorithmic thinking, optimal runtime/space complexity analysis (Big O), and problem-solving skills across arrays, strings, trees, and graphs.

inferred_topics.name: Object-Oriented Design (OOD)
inferred_topics.why_interview_relevant: Amazon SDE-1 interviews feature a dedicated Low-Level Design (LLD) / OOD round. Candidates are evaluated on SOLID principles, design patterns (Factory, Singleton, Strategy, Observer), and writing clean, modular class interfaces.

inferred_topics.name: Amazon Leadership Principles (LPs)
inferred_topics.why_interview_relevant: LPs (e.g., Customer Obsession, Ownership, Bias for Action, Learn and Be Curious) form 50% of the interview evaluation weight. Candidates must present past engineering experiences structured in the STAR format.

inferred_topics.name: Concurrency & Multithreading
inferred_topics.why_interview_relevant: Handling real-time media streams and processing parallel video/audio requests requires robust concurrency management. Tests understanding of thread pools, locks, race conditions, and synchronized operations.

inferred_topics.name: REST API Security & Scalability
inferred_topics.why_interview_relevant: Evaluates how the candidate structures client-server communications, manages sessions/authentication (e.g., JWT), handles request throttling, and optimizes large file uploads (such as audio/video recordings).

weak_or_missing_areas: No cloud platform (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure) usage listed, which is a major expectation for engineering at Amazon. The candidate should expect questions on cloud storage (e.g., S3 for video storage) and hosting.
Lack of detail on automated testing frameworks (JUnit, Mockito) for Spring Boot applications.
No concrete details regarding the scale of the AI Interview System (e.g., performance metrics, concurrent session handling limits, database throughput).
recommended_preparation_topics: Practicing Amazon-specific LeetCode Medium/Hard algorithmic challenges, focusing heavily on Trees, Graphs, BFS/DFS, Heaps, and Dynamic Programming.
Drafting LP behavioral responses in the STAR format using the 'AI Interview System' project to highlight 'Ownership', 'Deliver Results', and 'Bias for Action'.
Studying typical Object-Oriented Design (OOD) interview questions (e.g., designing a Parking Lot, Movie Ticket Booking System, or Vending Machine).
Familiarizing with basic AWS architecture concepts (S3, EC2, RDS, Lambda) and how they could be used to host and scale the 'AI Interview System'.
